findings: The primary specimen is a single complete Golden-crowned Kinglet with one head, one bill, one tail, two convincingly attached legs and feet, and a complete wing pair with the far-side wing naturally occluded by the profile pose.
The detached wing and head are clearly separated supplementary studies rather than duplicate parts attached to the primary specimen; both are anatomically coherent.
The primary and supplementary heads have proportionate, pointed bills with consistently rendered, essentially co-terminal mandibles matching the side-profile field references.
The eye placement and size, rounded body, relatively large head, short wings, skinny tail, slender dark legs, and yellowish feet agree with the references and direct identification guidance.

The plate correctly depicts an adult male pattern: a yellow crown with an orange center bordered by black, a black-and-white striped face, olive-gray upperparts, pale grayish-white underparts, dark flight feathers with yellow edging, and a white wingbar.
The illustrated crown is raised and conspicuous but remains compatible with an adult male; the attached references also show variable crown exposure.
The common name, scientific name, and family are correctly printed as Golden-crowned Kinglet, Regulus satrapa, and Regulidae.

The printed length, weight, and wingspan values exactly match the compatible published All About Birds measurement set for both sexes: 3.1–4.3 in (8–11 cm), 0.1–0.3 oz (4–8 g), and 5.5–7.1 in (14–18 cm).
The habitat and behavior paragraphs are coherent, correctly spelled, and consistent with the direct sources.
Every field-mark bullet is legible, grammatically complete, and supported by the direct sources and attached photographs.

The vertical ruler increases correctly from 3.1 in (8 cm) at the bottom to 4.3 in (11 cm) at the top, agrees with the printed body-length range, contains no contradictory marker, and is explicitly labeled “SCHEMATIC — NOT TO SCALE.”
The repeated bottom caption, “BODY LENGTH: Both sexes: 3.1–4.3 in (8–11 cm),” agrees with both the measurement block and ruler endpoints.
No place name, ZIP code, coordinates, map, range map, or local-observation detail appears.
The layout is balanced and readable, with the primary specimen clearly dominant and the supplementary studies, palette, ruler, and text visually distinct.
